tips.endpointUrl: Base URL or full path both work (e.g. https://api.example.com or …/v1/chat/completions). Non-v1 versions like /v4 are supported.
tips.apiKey: Optional — leave blank for a raw endpoint that needs no auth, and no Authorization header is sent. Stored encrypted at rest, never in plaintext. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed: a key that is only spaces is treated as no key.
tips.summary: One line — shown on the leaderboard next to your entry.
tips.detail: Markdown supported — rendered on the submission detail page.
tips.concurrency: Overrides the concurrency of every module that has one (clamped to each module's allowed range). Leave blank to keep each module's configured value.
tips.concurrencyModes: Overrides module concurrency for this run: either one global value applied to every module that has a concurrency setting, or individual per-module values (each clamped to the module's allowed range). The two modes are mutually exclusive; keep "Module defaults" to change nothing.
tips.hardware: The hardware this model was served on. Optional, but without it the card-normalized throughput metrics assume the endpoint is already at the baseline card count.
tips.concurrencySingle: Overrides this module's concurrency, if it has one (clamped to its allowed range). Leave blank to keep the module's configured value.
tips.hardwareRecorded: The hardware this model was served on. Recorded with the run.
tips.contributor: A display name to list this submission under — a team, or the automation that ran it. Leave blank to use your account name.

replayDs.subtitle: Rolling replay datasets collected from live gateway traffic. A benchmark's replay module can track a profile instead of a fixed file.
replayDs.noCollector: No collector service is configured (DATASET_BUILDER_URL is unset), so profiles can be edited but nothing will build them.
replayDs.pinHint: Each submission pins one build for its whole run and records it, so a result can always be traced to the dataset that produced it. To make a build permanent (a rolling build is eventually pruned), Freeze it under Show builds — that promotes it to a static file listed below, whose path you paste into a dataset_source=fixed benchmark.
replayDs.noBuildYet: No build has been published yet — a benchmark pointed at this profile will fail until one is.
replayDs.freezePrompt: Freeze build {build} into a permanent dataset. Enter a name (lowercase slug) — the frozen file survives retention and can be replayed with dataset_source=fixed:
replayDs.downloadHint: Download this build's dataset file as published ({size}). Gzipped JSONL, byte-identical to what a run replays.
replayDs.prunedHint: Retention has removed this build's file from the datasets volume; only the history row remains. Freeze a build to keep it permanently.
replayDs.frozenSubtitle: Builds promoted to permanent, static files. Retention never touches these, so a benchmark set to dataset_source=fixed with one of these paths replays the exact same dataset every time.
replayDs.frozenEmpty: No frozen datasets. Use Freeze on a completed build above to make one permanent.
replayDs.frozenDeleteConfirm: Delete the frozen dataset "{name}"? This removes the file from the datasets volume.
replayDs.frozenInUseConfirm: The frozen dataset "{name}" is still referenced by: {benchmarks}. Deleting it will make those benchmarks fall back to the worker's default dataset. Delete anyway?
replayDs.fNameHint: Lowercase slug; names the directory on the datasets volume and cannot be changed later.
replayDs.fModelsHint: Comma-separated, exact match on the model field (not a text search, so glm-5 will not match glm-5.2).
replayDs.fForwardedToHint: Comma-separated backend URLs. Pin one to keep the dataset to a single machine's traffic.
replayDs.fExtraHint: Optional raw LogsQL, AND-ed with the filters above.
replayDs.fExcludeTruncated: Skip captures whose request body was truncated (unreplayable)
replayDs.probeMatched: {n} matching records in the last hour
replayDs.fSubwindowHint: The window is sampled slice by slice, so the daily traffic mix is preserved.
replayDs.fOversampleHint: How many candidates to fetch per kept record; higher costs more download but survives a heavy drop rate.
replayDs.fMaxCarryHint: A single sub-window keeps at most base_quota × this. Raise it when traffic is concentrated in a few slices, or the sample can't reach the target size.
replayDs.sliceCapLine: {slices} slices · base quota {base}/slice · per-slice cap = {base} × {mult} = {cap} records kept per slice.
replayDs.sliceCapReach: Traffic spanning fewer than {need} slices cannot reach the target sample size — raise the carry multiple, sample size, or sub-window length.
replayDs.fClean: Clean requests for a strict backend (drop over-context and broken records, clamp max_tokens)
replayDs.fMaxModelLenHint: The context window of the endpoints this dataset will be replayed against.
replayDs.fMinRecordsHint: A build below this is discarded and the previous one keeps serving.
replayDs.fMinBucketsHint: Rejects a build too narrow to exercise the per-length TTFT thresholds.
replayDs.fKeepRespBody: Keep the captured response body (roughly doubles dataset size; not used by replay)
replayDs.fCompress: Store builds gzipped (about 3.6x smaller; readers decompress transparently)
replayDs.fIntervalHint: 0 = manual only (rebuilt only when the API is called).
replayDs.fAnchorHourHint: Local hour to build at; -1 for no anchor.
replayDs.fMaxAgeHint: Older builds still run, but the run is flagged stale.
replayDs.fMinRetainHint: Must exceed the longest replay run, or retention could delete a dataset out from under one.
replayDs.deleteConfirm: Delete the collection profile "{name}"? Published dataset files are left on disk.
replayDs.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard
replayDs.fSourceUrlHintFiles: The directory the gateway's bodylog listener writes, mounted into the collector (file:///data/bodylog).
replayDs.fSourceUrlHintVl: The VictoriaLogs base URL the gateway's bodylogs are shipped to.

metricTips.input_tpm_card_norm: Input tokens per minute, normalized to 8 cards: raw input TPM × 8 ÷ total card count (cards per machine × machine count from the Hardware section; assumed 8 if not provided). A 4-card endpoint's value is doubled, so differently-sized deployments compare fairly.
metricTips.output_tpm_card_norm: Output tokens per minute, normalized to 8 cards: raw output TPM × 8 ÷ total card count (cards per machine × machine count from the Hardware section; assumed 8 if not provided). A 4-card endpoint's value is doubled, so differently-sized deployments compare fairly.
metricTips.cached_tpm_card_norm: Cached prompt tokens per minute, normalized to 8 cards: raw cached TPM × 8 ÷ total card count (from the Hardware section; assumed 8 if not provided). A subset of input TPM — not additive with it.
metricTips.total_tpm_card_norm: Total (input + output) tokens per minute, normalized to 8 cards: raw total TPM × 8 ÷ total card count (from the Hardware section; assumed 8 if not provided). A 4-card endpoint's value is doubled, so differently-sized deployments compare fairly.
